confidence_notes: The RBA rate comes from a search of RBA pages. The latest observation I found was 2026-11-18, and I did not find one for 19 Nov. Food and drink anchors are based on aggregated, crowd-sourced cost-of-living indexes (Numbeo data via Expatica, June 2026; MyLifeElsewhere; Expat Arrivals). Those put an inexpensive meal at about ¥1,000-1,200, a domestic draught beer at about ¥550, a cappuccino at about ¥530 and a three-course meal for two at about ¥7,000. I converted yen to USD at roughly ¥155/USD, an approximation inferred from the MyLifeElsewhere page. Cocktail and wine have weak direct data. The cocktail is set at about 2.4x the beer price (about ¥1,300), which sits below one Expatistan guess of about ¥2,000 for a downtown club. The wine glass is set at about ¥900, a middle value between cheap chain prices and the ¥1,000+ seen at typical restaurants. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for Tokyo, not from live listings. They are the least certain anchors, and prices swing widely by season and area.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tokyo is estimated directly from Tokyo price indexes. Accommodation uses general knowledge of Tokyo's hostel, business-hotel and three-star market, which is moderately priced for a major world city but elevated by recent tourism demand and a weak yen.
